title: Fleet throttle & surge adjuster UI: interactive capacity knobs, predictive throughput charts, and change stream
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Build an operator-facing Console surface that exposes 'throttle' and 'surge' controls for Dedicated fleets. The goal is a single place where operators can: tune throughput guarantees, configure autoscaling policies (min/max/scale-step/cooldown), preview cost/latency impact, simulate traffic scenarios, and review an auditable change stream with diffs and rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: UI provides live adjustable knobs for per-fleet throughput target and burst capacity (throttle / surge) and persists to fleet spec
Autoscaling policy editor supports scheduled rules, utilization-based rules, and emergency manual override with clear priority semantics
Predictive charts show 24h latency/throughput/cost forecasts after a change and an estimated token-cost delta
Change stream records every operator action with user, timestamp, before/after spec diff, and an optional rollout note
Operators can run a simulation applying a change against recent traffic (last 1h) and see predicted SLO breaches and cost impact before commit
Support rollbacks to any prior fleet spec from change history and surface potential risk warnings
All interactions are accessible (keyboard + screen reader) and follow Redwood Console design system tokens
qa_plan: End-to-end QA with: unit tests for editor validation; integration tests for persistence and rollback; load-tested simulation backend using anonymized traffic; accessibility audit. QA checklist stored in /qa/capacity-throttle/checklist.md
rollout_plan: Beta rollout to 10 pilot fleets (internal + 2 customers) -> collect telemetry for 2 weeks -> open to all Dedicated orgs behind feature flag -> enable by default in next minor release if no regressions
